decisions.summary: Form decided by count compared: --seeds/--households comma lists (defaults 25, 40); one seed one size QUICK N=6, more SUBSET N=3, --full FULL N=3 with make perf SCALING=1's seeds and sizes; Makefile passes SEEDS/HOUSEHOLDS/FULL/N/AA.
decisions.why: Restates FR-001 and the approved proposal's three steps (quick default seed 25 at 40 households, 6 runs; subset SEEDS=25,39 HOUSEHOLDS=20,40; full = today's sweep).

decisions.summary: Quick and subset roll in one warmed worker process per version inside that version's worktree, calling the version's own perf_snapshot.measure per run over stdin; calls counted once after; FULL keeps today's fresh-process make perf SCALING=1 path.
decisions.why: The request and proposal ask for 6 runs of a single seed per version and do not prescribe the process model; timing with each version's own code and warming as make perf warms is an implementation choice that removes nothing asked. FULL is left as today's sweep per FR-001. Engines predating d2ce4e79c lack the functions used; comparing such old engines is not part of the request and the FR-005 escape remains for them.

decisions.summary: Run i takes A,B when even, B,A when odd.
decisions.why: Exactly the proposal's 'A then B, then B then A' and FR-003.

decisions.summary: Wall = sum of stages, CPU = sum of cpu_stages, to the hundredth; per seed and size best and spread (worst less best) of each, change between versions, and calls.
decisions.why: Carries the GM's 'CPU time beside wall time' and the proposal's 'each with its best and spread' (FR-003).

decisions.summary: Quick record at <git common dir>/perf-ab/quick/<sorted pair of engine_fingerprint keys>.json, local, never committed, holding seed, size, N, commits, table.
decisions.why: FR-004: local, never pushed, under both engines' code keys ignoring docstrings/comments; the proposal's 'same two engines judged by the engine code, not the commit name'. Sorting the pair treats 'the same two engines' symmetrically, which the words already imply.

decisions.summary: Non-quick runs look up D5's record after worktrees are made and before the first roll; with none and no PERF_AB_QUICK_OK, print a refusal naming the quick command and exit 2; the escape goes through escape_log.escape (reason of two words or more, logged as guard perf-ab-quick-first); a timing never refuses.
decisions.why: FR-005 (before any roll, names the quick command, escape with stated reason recorded where escapes are recorded) and FR-007 (refuses a skipped step, never a timing). The two-word minimum is the project's existing escape mechanism giving 'a stated reason' its form, not a new carve-out; it applies to all non-quick forms with no exception.

decisions.summary: AA=1 builds one worktree of A (default HEAD), two alternating workers, writes perf-ab/floor/<seed>-<households>-<n>.json; a quick comparison prints that floor beside its table, or the AA=1 command to take it when none exists; AA=1 is a quick-form run needing no record.
decisions.why: FR-006 and the proposal's 'A/A run of the quick form taken once and printed beside each quick result'. Printing the command when no floor exists is the accepted spec's mechanism (AA=1 takes it); AA=1 not needing a quick record follows from it being a quick form, not an exception to the refusal.

decisions.summary: performance-checklist question 5 and tools table: quick while iterating, subset or full once before landing, floor read beside quick; guards.md gains the refusal row with escape; Makefile help line names the forms.
decisions.why: FR-008 and the proposal's checklist line; the help line only documents the requested forms.

decisions.id: Performance bookends / Constitution Check / T01 approach
decisions.summary: No engine code changed, no bookends; tests in tests/tools/test_perf_ab.py, 100% coverage, guard doctrine; T01 done = a real quick A/B of HEAD~ vs HEAD at seed 25/40 with wall time stated and the refusal seen on a subset run without a record.
decisions.why: Verification and enforcement of exactly what was asked; the one figure with a unit (8.2 min) carries a one-shot label (2026-10-27, file times of feature 435's T04/T08 logs).
